A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PrITTI research work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original KITTI-360 reconstruction and generation experiments, architectural ablations, synthetic encoding experiments, and qualitative editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Argoverse 2 results, GPU-memory measurements, additional conditioning examples, and a nearest-neighbor analysis.

M1.justification: The primitive representation, Cholesky encoding, split-latent VAE, conditional DiT, losses, and editing procedures are retained. Vehicle-density, joint-density, and Argoverse 2 experiments apply the existing procedure with different labels or category configurations; no new algorithmic component is described.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation on Argoverse 2, extending coverage beyond KITTI-360 and synthetic primitives to scenes with fewer annotated object categories (Appendix H, Table 9, Figure 13). It also evaluates vehicle-density and joint vegetation–vehicle conditioning, whereas v2 demonstrates vegetation-density conditioning.

E2.justification: The corresponding reconstruction, generation, editing, and extrapolation comparisons retain the same participating methods and variants, including SemCity, PDD, and XCube. The new memory comparison uses these existing baselines; Argoverse 2 results contain no baseline comparison.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols measure peak memory over 100 scenes with batch size one on a single GPU and compare 50K generated against 50K training samples using VGG16 nearest-neighbor distances, with self-matches excluded from the real-to-real control. Argoverse 2 uses 84 queries rather than KITTI-360's 514. Existing KITTI-360 settings remain; Section 4.1 drops the stated AP@0.25 metric, without removing a corresponding result column.

E4.justification: Appendix G and Figure 11 add a focused memorization analysis using generated-to-training and real-to-real nearest neighbors. Section B.2.4 also newly reports visually similar reconstructions across existence thresholds of 0.25–0.75. The existing architectural ablations, encoding comparison, and precision/recall sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed synthetic encoding experiment and retain Figure 4's variability display. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced. The new nearest-neighbor distance summaries describe diagnostic outcomes rather than estimation uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing KITTI-360 results remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear: Argoverse 2 AP3D 56.495 and FID 144.330 (Table 9); peak GPU memory of 0.89 GB for PrITTI versus 8.30, 1.33, and 4.84 GB for SemCity, PDD, and XCube (Table 8); and mean generated-to-training versus real-to-real distances of approximately 52.2 versus 22.5 (Appendix G). New conditioning examples also appear. These are additional evaluations, not improvements over v2 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The Cholesky construction and its mathematical properties, VAE objectives, diffusion derivations, latent-editing equations, and precision/recall definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims concerning primitive-based generation, disentangled latents, Cholesky encoding, efficiency, and editability. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explains applicability with incomplete category coverage, interprets nearest-neighbor results as evidence against memorization, and discusses threshold and overlap tradeoffs. Its expanded limitations distinguish plausible from implausible primitive intersections and identify buildings intersecting roads. The explanation attributing faster inference to compact latents is also softened from a definite attribution to a possible one.

D1.justification: v3 documents Argoverse 2's seven category groups and 84 queries, clarifies that the existing 0.3 existence threshold is global, and specifies 50% overlap in all outpainting experiments. It further explains parallel generation within each outpainting pass. The abstract replaces the code-and-model availability statement with source code and additional results; this does not establish that model access was withdrawn.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained; Argoverse 2 was already cited in v2. Appendix D's expanded baseline rationale restates the existing primitive-versus-voxel distinction rather than introducing a new novelty claim or research comparison.

P1.justification: There are targeted wording, affiliation, and acknowledgment edits, expanded implementation explanations, and new appendix sections for overfitting and applicability beyond KITTI-360. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact; subsequent appendix sections are renumbered.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial new displays: GPU-memory and Argoverse 2 tables (Tables 8–9), a generated-versus-nearest-neighbors panel (Figure 11), and galleries for Argoverse 2, vehicle-density conditioning, and joint-density conditioning (Figures 13, 16–17). Existing figures and tables are retained, with relocation, renumbering, and layout reflow rather than replacement.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through Argoverse 2 evaluation, broader conditioning demonstrations, direct GPU-memory measurements, and a memorization diagnostic, while preserving the original results. More concrete failure explanations also improve transparency. The overall gain is limited: Argoverse 2 lacks baseline comparisons and explicit split/sample-count details, while nearest-neighbor distances provide indirect evidence against memorization. These additions improve validation without substantially resolving the remaining evaluation limitations.
